## Today's Dad Joke

What do organizational communication scholars say at the end of the semester?

<span class="fragment">Communication constitutes the conclusion.</span>

## Housekeeping

> - Final Paper due *yesterday* (Monday Dec 7)
> - Self-Assessment Reflection 3 due Friday Dec 11
> - Presentations today (Part 1) and Thursday (Part 2)

## Presentation Format

> - No more than 5 minutes per person
> - Q&A after each presentation
> - Be a good audience: engaged, specific questions, no phones

## What We're Looking For

> - A clear organizational communication *problem* or *phenomenon*
> - At least one theoretical framework applied — not just named
> - Evidence from your fieldwork or research
> - A takeaway: so what? What would you recommend or what did you learn?

## Listening Guide

> - As you listen to each presentation, ask yourself:
>   - What framework are they using?
>   - What would *another* framework from this course see differently?
>   - What's the most interesting thing they found?

## Thursday

> - Final presentations (Part 2)
> - Course wrap-up and reflection
> - You've spent a semester learning to see organizations differently — what do you see now that you didn't before?
